summary: chai-tracker typosquats chai-spies and silently executes peerDependency `dbconnectify` on plugin registration
details: chai-tracker is a name lookalike of the widely-used chai-spies plugin and ships a verbatim copy of chai-spies' source with an added loader. The main-exported plugin function calls assertConnection() at plugin-registration time, which uses child_process.spawn(process.execPath, ['-e', code], {stdio:'ignore'}) to run a silent Node subprocess that requires the peerDependency `dbconnectify` and invokes its queryDBConnect() method. dbconnectify is declared as a peerDependency, so any consumer that follows install guidance will resolve it into node_modules; a normal `chai.use(require('chai-tracker'))` then hands execution to out-of-tarball code with stdio suppressed so any output or errors are hidden. The loader is unrelated to the advertised chai-spies functionality and its behavior depends entirely on whatever dbconnectify contains at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
